forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: West Sussex says funding is confirmed for 90% of its schools deficit but it cannot absorb the other 10%
news_drafts.lead:
West Sussex County Council has told its Communities, Highways and Environment Scrutiny Committee that funding is confirmed for 90% of its March 2026 dedicated schools grant deficit, the government grant that funds schools, with the deficit usually arising from support for children with special needs. The council says it "is not in a position to absorb the residual liability", the remaining 10%.

The medium-term financial strategy report says plans to reform support for special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) have been approved. It says the government has not yet clarified the arrangements for 2026/27 and 2027/28. The paper describes the deficit as held off the council's balance sheet and as a significant risk to its long-term financial sustainability. The papers give no sum in pounds for the deficit or for the 10% left over.

Separately, the service pressures appendix shows SEND home to school transport with a projected in-year deficit of £6m for 2026/27. The same appendix lists a further £4m of annual demand growth for pupils with SEND on that service.

news_drafts.headline: West Sussex: funding confirmed for 90% of March 2026 schools deficit; 10% remains unresolved
news_drafts.lead:
Funding is confirmed for 90% of West Sussex County Council's dedicated schools grant (DSG) deficit balance as at March 2026, according to the council's medium term financial strategy papers for the Health and Adult Social Care Scrutiny Committee meeting on 19 November. The DSG is the government grant that funds schools, and a deficit on it is usually an overspend on support for children with special needs. The other 10% of the balance is still unresolved.

The paper says the council is not in a position to absorb that residual liability. It also says the lack of government clarity on arrangements for 2026/27 and 2027/28 presents a risk to long-term financial sustainability. The DSG deficit is held off the council's balance sheet.

The same strategy papers list pressures for 2027/28 in the children, young people and learning block. One line is £6.0m for home to school transport for children with special educational needs and disabilities, labelled a projected in-year deficit for 2026/27. A separate line shows annual growth of £4.0m for the same service.

news_drafts.headline: West Sussex has government funding confirmed for 90% of its March 2026 schools deficit; 10% is unresolved
news_drafts.lead:
Government funding is confirmed for 90% of West Sussex County Council's dedicated schools grant (DSG) deficit as it stood in March 2026, the council's medium-term financial strategy report says. The DSG is the government grant that funds schools; its deficit here is an overspend on support for children with special educational needs. The paper says the SEND (special educational needs and disabilities) reform plans have been approved. The remaining 10% is described as uncertain, with no government clarity on arrangements for 2026/27 and 2027/28. The paper says the deficit is held off the council's balance sheet.

The Children and Young People's Services Scrutiny Committee meets on 18 November. Its papers show SEND home to school transport with a £6m projected deficit for 2026/27, listed as an in-year pressure. The same paper lists £4m of annual growth for the service. Both lines are attributed to demand from pupils with SEND.

A supplementary paper from the Children, Young People and Learning directorate names four areas as its most significant pressures: placements for children the council cares for, SEND, home to school transport, and unaccompanied asylum-seeking children. It attributes them to rising demand, increasing complexity of need and national reforms.

findings.committee: Communities, Highways and Environment Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: Fire and rescue transfer to the Sussex and Brighton Strategic Authority from April 2027 is expected to be financially neutral for 2027/28
findings.detail: Work is underway to set the cost of the service and the funding to transfer, including a share of core funding and council tax. The paper says the effect will be reflected in future reports once the detailed arrangements are finalised.
findings.matters: A transfer of a service and its funding to a new strategic authority changes the base the council's future budget is built on.
findings.quote: As the transfer is expected to be financially neutral to the County Council in 2027/28

findings.committee: Communities, Highways and Environment Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: The budget assumes a 4.99% council tax rise, with each 1% worth approximately £6.8m
findings.detail: Council tax is about 80% of the council's net revenue budget. The paper assumes a 0.5% taxbase increase, and final confirmation will come from the district and borough councils in January 2027. The formal decision on the increase is reserved for the February 2027 County Council meeting.
findings.matters: The reliance on the maximum council tax increase to balance the budget is a lever that other councils facing the same referendum limits will compare.
findings.figures: 4.99% assumed increase; approximately £6.8m per 1%; £719.4m council tax income for 2027/28; about 80% of net revenue budget
findings.quote: every 1% increase equates to approximately £6.8m of additional income

findings.committee: Communities, Highways and Environment Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: The Fair Funding Assessment falls from £226.5m in 2026/27 to £207.8m in 2028/29
findings.detail: The paper attributes the reduction to the 2026/27 Fair Funding Review 2.0, which reset business rates retention and updated relative-need allocations. The three-year settlement gives greater certainty, but the paper says it does not address the structural gap in social care funding.
findings.matters: A multi-year cut to core funding in a council already overspending is a structural revenue change that peer councils facing the same reform will be modelling.
findings.quote: the implementation of FFR 2.0 results in a reduction in the County Council

findings.committee: Communities, Highways and Environment Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: The paper says reserves may again be required to support the 2026/27 year-end position
findings.detail: The paper says the Q1 Performance and Resources Report already projects an overspend, so reserves may again be needed for the outturn. The medium-term forecast makes no provision for ongoing use of reserves to support the revenue budget. The Section 151 Officer will assess reserve adequacy in January 2027.
findings.matters: Reliance on reserves to close an in-year overspend, after a forecast that assumes none, is the sequence a finance director at another council would watch closely.
findings.quote: there remains a risk that reserves may again be required to support the outturn position at the end of the year.

findings.committee: Communities, Highways and Environment Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: Funding is confirmed for 90% of the March 2026 DSG deficit balance, and the council says it cannot absorb the 10% residual liability
findings.detail: The paper says the SEND reform plans have been approved and that the Government has not yet clarified arrangements for 2026/27 and 2027/28. It describes the DSG deficit as held off-balance sheet and as a significant risk to long-term financial sustainability.
findings.matters: An off-balance-sheet deficit with an unresolved 10% residual exposure is a contingent liability that lenders and peer finance directors will want to see resolved.
findings.figures: 90% of the March 2026 DSG deficit balance confirmed; 10% residual liability
findings.quote: The County Council is not in a position to absorb the residual liability

daily_post.headline: West Sussex Pension Fund says its future liquidity arrangements are yet to be defined in response to the Government's Fit for the Future policy
daily_post.lead: Pool and liquidity arrangements for LGPS funds are changing nationally, and a finance director at another council needs to know which parts of their own fund's cash management are still open.
